Container.Name: wellnessquest
Container.Overview:
WellnessQuest — a two-person wellness tracker with a Home Assistant adapter.
This single container serves: • the PWA at / • the REST API + HA webhook adapter at /api/v1/* • the OpenAPI/Swagger docs at /docs
Bring your own Postgres 16. Set DATABASE_URL below to point at it (a separate container, a VM, or anything reachable from this container's network). On every start the container runs Alembic migrations and then the idempotent seed script, so the configured Postgres user needs CREATE privileges on the target database.
First boot creates the ADMIN_* user (and PARTNER_* if a partner password is set) using the values below. The seed only creates missing users — once a user exists in Postgres, changing ADMIN_PASSWORD here will NOT rotate the stored password; change it from the UI instead, or delete the row and let the next start re-seed.
First-time secret generation:
python3 -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))" # JWT_SECRET python3 -c "from cryptography.fernet import Fernet; print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())" # FERNET_KEY
Container.Requires: A reachable Postgres 16 server (host:port + user/password/db) and GHCR auth for the private package (`docker login ghcr.io`). See docs/unraid.md.

Config.Name: App port
Config.Description: Host port that maps to the unified container. Browse to http://<unraid-ip>:<this-port>/ to reach the PWA and /api/v1/* for the API.

Config.Name: DATABASE_URL
Config.Description: SQLAlchemy async DSN to your Postgres 16. Format: postgresql+asyncpg://USER:PASSWORD@HOST:PORT/DBNAME. HOST can be an Unraid container name (only if you've placed both this container and your Postgres on the same custom docker network), an IP, or a hostname. The user must already exist and have rights to CREATE on DBNAME — Alembic builds the schema on startup. Example: postgresql+asyncpg://wq:hunter2@192.168.1.10:5432/wellnessquest

Config.Name: JWT_SECRET
Config.Description: 32+ byte random string used to sign access tokens. Generate with: python3 -c 'import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))'

Config.Name: FERNET_KEY
Config.Description: Fernet key used to encrypt long-lived Home Assistant tokens at rest. Generate with: python3 -c 'from cryptography.fernet import Fernet; print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())'

Config.Name: CORS_ORIGINS
Config.Description: Comma-separated allow-list for browser CORS. Same-origin requests from the bundled PWA do not need to appear here; only add additional origins if you proxy the app behind a different hostname (e.g. https://wq.example.com) or hit the API directly from another web app. Home Assistant is not a browser and ignores CORS.

Config.Name: ADMIN_EMAIL
Config.Description: Email for the first user the seed script creates. Only read during `python -m app.db.seed`; afterwards the user lives in Postgres.

Config.Name: ADMIN_PASSWORD
Config.Description: Initial admin password. Argon2-hashed by the seed script; rotate it from the UI after first login.

Config.Name: PARTNER_EMAIL
Config.Description: Email for the second seeded user (optional).

Config.Name: PARTNER_PASSWORD
Config.Description: Initial password for the partner user (optional). Leave blank to skip seeding a second user.

Config.Name: ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS
Config.Description: JWT access-token lifetime in seconds (default 15 min).

Config.Name: TZ
Config.Description: IANA timezone for streak and day-rollover calculations.

Config.Name: LOG_LEVEL
Config.Description: Python logging level (DEBUG / INFO / WARNING / ERROR).
